column3: The Hebrew asks whether anyone answers, rather than who will answer.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says I cursed his dwelling; BSB says his house was cursed.
The Hebrew names the gate; BSB interprets it as court.
The Hebrew ends with their wealth, using a plural possessor; BSB says his wealth.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew pictures sparks as sons of flame and joins the clauses with and rather than an explicit comparison.
The Hebrew says I without explicitly adding if I were you; it names God twice.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew pictures the earth’s and fields’ surfaces as their faces.
The Hebrew begins with a purpose, to set the lowly on high; BSB makes this an independent action.
The Hebrew describes what their hands do, rather than finding success.
The Hebrew describes their counsel as hasty; BSB says He sweeps away their plans.
